messages:
maria: FYI saw a sustained backlog on west-1-gpu pool around 03:12 UTC, queue length > 600 for ~8m. admission controller started dropping but we still hit tail latency spikes. :warning:
aj: Ugh. Any obvious culprit? model churn, big batch jobs, or network flakiness?
devon: logs look like a lot of client retries. I see repetitive 429s followed by immediate retries — looks like a retry storm.
maria: Exactly. The token bucket was exhausted per-pool, but clients retried aggressively and kept us saturated. Also observed a regional fallback path spinning new requests into the same pool.
lina: Can you paste the admission metrics? especially token refill rate, effective TPM, and EWMA of inflight?
maria: Paste from dashboard scrubbed: 
```
pool: west-1-gpu
tokens.capacity: 120000 (pool total)
refill.per_sec: 33.3
steady_tpm_capacity: 120000 * 60? wait the math we use is tokens == tokens_per_min? Rough notes: tokens represent token-equivalents, our controller maps request_cost -> tokens and refills tokens per second.
EWMA_inflight: 210 -> 480 over 6m
queue_len: 620 -> 140
429_rate: 18% peak
```
aj: That refill looks low when EWMA jumps. Are we smoothing too aggressively? EWMA window might be too long so our controller under-reacts to spikes, letting queue build then triggers hard drops.
devon: Also penalty loop: when we drop, clients backoff poorly and then some tiers fallback to alternate region, which routes back here due to DNS weight, amplifying the spike.
lina: Two attack vectors: (1) admission hysteresis — increase upper/lower thresholds to avoid flip-flopping; (2) penalize immediate retries at edge via short token holdout for repeat offenders.
maria: I'm worried about fairness across customers. If we hold tokens for retries, multi-tenant jumbo customer could hog. Need per-customer tokens + global cap.
aj: Proposed quick changes to test in staging: 
- reduce EWMA half-life from 60s -> 20s so refill adapts faster
- add a small hysteresis window: only change admission state if metric crosses threshold for 15s
- per-client retry-penalty: after a 429, mark client with penalty score and increase cost multiplier for 5s (multiplicative backoff)
- jitter client-facing Retry-After header suggestions
```
// pseudo-config
admission:
  ewma_half_life: 20s
  hysteresis_ms: 15000
  penalty:
    enabled: true
    base_multiplier: 2.0
    duration_ms: 5000
```
devon: Also add token-bucket top-up pulses for short bursts: allow a 10% burst credit that decays if sustained. That reduces tail spikes without permanently raising capacity.
lina: Simulation numbers? If pool capacity is 120k tokens and average request = 100 tokens, steady_tpm = (120k / 100) * 60 = 72k RPM? That math feels off. We should simulate at request-cost distribution.
maria: I ran a quick sim locally with our request cost histogram (p50=85, p95=420):
- baseline: EWMA=60s, no penalty -> tail 99th latency 1200ms, peak queue 780
- proposed: EWMA=20s + penalty + burst 10% -> 99th latency 420ms, peak queue 180
small sample but promising.
aj: Nice. Two operational concerns: (1) cost — burst credits allow higher instantaneous GPU usage -> bill spike; (2) complexity of per-client penalty state in control plane.
nina: (typo: lina) we can keep penalty state sharded by customer and TTL-based; that's cheap. For cost we can gate burst credits behind reserved capacity or higher plan.
devon: Also need network view: we saw a couple of 5xx patterns from node-local proxy earlier — chasing that in parallel. If proxy retransmits, it looks like client retries.
sre-bot: incident-created: INC-2026 spike-west1-2026-03-12. Pager duty triggered, channel: #incidents, priority: p2.
maria: OK plan:
- short rollout to staging of admission tweaks (EWMA/hysteresis/penalty) today 16:00 PT
- simulate heavy retry patterns with our replay harness (devon)
- if improvement -> canary to 10% traffic in west-1 tomorrow
- ops: add temporary guardrail to disable regional fallback if pool queue > 500
aj: I'll own the config change PR and metrics dashboards for hysteresis.
devon: I'll run the replay and also drop a small probe that forces clients to respect Retry-After with jitter.
lina: I'll add per-customer token accounting to the design doc, include cost implications, and sketch the fairness algorithm.
maria: Thanks. If we still see a spike after these, next steps: tighten routing (no regional fallback), throttle client SDKs centrally, and consider prewarming extra nodes. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: deploy started: admission-config-v2 -> staging (maria/aj)
maria: ping @aj when deploy completes, I'll kick off replay.
aj: will do. :eyes:
